articles.title: Minecraft Dungeons 2 gets a September release date
articles.summary: Microsoft shared new information about Minecraft Dungeons 2.
articles.body: Minecraft Dungeons 2, a sequel to Microsoft’s dungeon crawler spinoff Minecraft Dungeons, will be released on September 29th. The company originally revealed the game in a brief trailer in March, promising a fall 2026 release window. Here’s how Microsoft described it at the time: > Return to the world of Minecraft Dungeons in an all new action RPG adventure, brimming with high stakes encounters, thrilling challenges, and never before seen locations, as you set out to save a world in crisis. Will you and your allies prevail against the forces of evil and save the day once more? Minecraft Dungeons 2 will be available on Nintendo Switch, Nintendo Switch 2, PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X / S. The original Minecraft Dungeons launched in 2020, with my colleague Andrew Webster calling it a “lighter, more family-friendly take on Diablo.” There’s no mining or crafting in the game; instead, you tackle dungeons and loot cool gear.

articles.title: 'Gaming pays me double what I earned as a teacher'
articles.summary: Jarvs Tasker says it would have taken her 20 years as a teacher to make what she earns now.
articles.body:
In 2019, Jarvs Tasker was forced to give up her teaching career due to chronic illness when she was just 28.

Fast forward seven years, and she earns double her former annual salary, running Jarvs Indie Insights, which provides communication and marketing within the gaming industry.

She visited the University of Suffolk's e-sport building in Ipswich to celebrate independent game developers and studios on Wednesday.

"I can comfortably say it probably would have taken me about 20 years in teaching to earn what I make now," she said.

When Tasker left teaching, she initially started volunteering for PlayStation's YouTube channel, but she said there was lots of crossover between the two industries.

"Managing a community is very similar to managing a class of kids, so there's a lot of crossover skills there, but actually, video games is one of those industries where a lot of people come into it later on in life."

Tasker, who lives in Exeter, believed young people might not know the "many pathways" available in the industry.

"The video games community is very strong, and they will champion people that love what they do, but they'll also notice if you're in it just for the money," she continued.

Asked about the impact of AI, she said she believed the industry was doing a "really great job" at rejecting it, because players hated it.

"I think as an industry we should be really proud of the fact that we're still championing human creativity and that the audience is also on board with that," she added.

Tasker had been in Suffolk as part of an event hosted by Game Anglia to showcase the growing independent gaming industry in the East of England.

Mark Backler from Game Anglia said the industry was now one of the biggest in the UK , and while he agreed it was competitive, it was "more possible than ever to develop and release your own independent games".

"It's like being a content creator - it's tricky to be one of the standout ones, but it is doable," he said.

He added it was difficult to tell how AI would change things, but a lot of players were against its use.

Sam Read-Graves is a developer at Read Graves and works specifically in the East.

At the event, he said the gaming industry had "grown massively in the past 10 years".

"Because of schemes like Game Anglia across Suffolk, Essex, Cambridgeshire, Norfolk, there are really great clusters of a lot of students and a lot of developers, and I like to think that this has started to bring in studios who could make the big games.

"When it comes to those games like Call of Duty or FIFA, those at the minute aren't going to come out of the East of England because we don't have big studios.

"But when it comes to independent developers, there's no reason those games can't financially be as big."

Abbygale Dunn, 22, is the founder and director of Astral Forge, an independent game development company based in Essex.

She said there was "so much space for women" in the industry today.

"It's obviously daunting. When I studied, there were only about three women in my course," she said.

"Everyone is so kind; it's really not as bad as it seems, especially nowadays.

"As a programmer myself, which is more rare for women to be in, I've never felt out of place."

Omar Khalil is game scout lead at Entity and said there was "no shortage of talent in the UK", but it was challenging to create the next big game.

"There are so many games out there right now, and it's not like there aren't enough good games; it's how do you get visibility on those games?" he explained.

Additional reporting by Alice Cunningham.

articles.title: Corsair Gaming Headsets See Early Prime Big Deal Days Discounts on Amazon UK
articles.summary: Save early on Corsair gaming headsets at Amazon UK ahead of Prime Big Deal Days, featuring wireless VOID v2 and wired HS65 SURROUND models.
articles.body:
Amazon's Prime Big Deal Days doesn't officially kick off until October 6, but we're already seeing some early discounts ahead of the two-day event, including savings on a couple of Corsair's gaming headsets.

Right now, you can pick up the Corsair VOID v2 wireless headset for £69.99 or the wired Corsair HS65 SURROUND for £72.78 at Amazon UK. Neither deal is officially part of Prime Big Deal Days yet, but if you've been looking for a new gaming headset, they're worth checking out before the main event gets underway.

Let's start with the Corsair VOID v2 , which is down to £69.99 at Amazon UK, a 30% saving.

It's a wireless headset with Corsair's distinctive styling, complete with lighting on the earcups, but there's more to it than looking the part. The VOID v2 packs Dolby Atmos Spatial Audio and custom-tuned 50mm drivers, designed to give you a better sense of where sounds are coming from in games.

That could mean picking up on a stealthy killer creeping around in Dead by Daylight , hearing where a grenade has landed in Battlefield 6 , or keeping track of proximity chat in ARC Raiders and Marathon .

Connectivity is another big selling point. The VOID v2 uses a 2.4GHz wireless dongle and Bluetooth, with support across PC, PlayStation, Nintendo Switch and mobile. You can switch between devices at the press of a button, which makes it a handy option if your gaming setup involves more than one platform.

Battery life is pretty impressive, too, with up to 70 hours of use on a full charge. Corsair says a quick 15-minute charge can also give you another six hours of playtime, which should be enough to get you through a particularly long gaming session.

If you'd rather keep things simple, the Corsair HS65 SURROUND is a wired alternative that's currently £72.78 at Amazon UK.

The benefit of a wired headset is that there's no battery to worry about, and the HS65 SURROUND can be plugged straight into compatible devices, including PS5, where it works with Sony's Tempest 3D AudioTech.

It also supports Dolby Atmos Spatial Audio and comes with memory foam earcups covered in leatherette, giving it a more premium feel than you might expect from a wired headset.

The microphone has flip-to-mute functionality, too, so you can quickly silence yourself without having to reach for a button when you're playing a game with proximity chat. That's particularly handy when you're trying not to accidentally broadcast whatever's happening in the room around you to everyone else in the lobby.

So, you've got a wireless headset with multi-platform connectivity and long battery life in the VOID v2, or a cheaper wired option in the HS65 SURROUND that doesn't need charging at all.

And while these aren't Prime Big Deal Days prices just yet, Amazon's main October sale is only around the corner. Prime Big Deal Days runs October 6-7 , so there's always a chance we'll see further reductions once the event officially begins.

articles.title: Don't Breathe 3 in the Works With Stephen Lang and Jane Levy, Fede Álvarez Says
articles.summary: Director Fede Álvarez has confirmed Don't Breathe 3 is in the works, with some of the cast from previous films expected to reprise their roles.
articles.body:
Director Fede Álvarez has confirmed Don't Breathe 3 is in the works, with some of the cast from previous films expected to reprise their roles.

The filmmaker behind some of the grislier horror movies of the last 15 years announced his intentions to finish his thriller trilogy with a proper third film at Beyond Fest 2026, as reported by Dread Central . Whether or not Álvarez will return as director is unclear, but it is said that he has at least returned to handle its script.

How the third Don't Breathe movie will materialize and what story it will tell remains unclear. However, it sounds like it will at least continue where the previous two films left off, with both Stephen Lang (Avatar) and Jane Levy (Evil Dead) expected to reprise their roles as The Blind Man a.k.a. Norman Nordstrom and Rocky, respectively.

Álvarez and Levy previously worked together on his 2013 Evil Dead reboot before re-teaming for the original Don't Breathe in 2016. The horror-thriller, which was also produced by scary movie visionary Sam Raimi , follows three thieves who break into a house before finding themselves fighting for their lives in a "lethal game of cat and mouse."

Don't Breathe 2 continued the story with Lang back as The Blind Man in 2021. The sequel saw Álvarez hand directing duties to frequent collaborator Rodo Sayagues, with Raimi also returning as producer. In the five years since its premiere, there have been few updates about how the crew might round out the trilogy with a Don't Breathe 3 despite Lang teasing a new movie through the years .

After diverting his attention to direct Alien: Romulus in 2024, Álvarez seems more ready than ever to round out the story. How far along he is in that process is unclear, though, so we'll have to wait to learn more about its release date or who else may be attached.

Álvarez has also reportedly been in the mix to produce an Alien: Romulus sequel , but its status is unclear . As the filmmaker continues to try to expand upon the Don't Breathe universe, you can read IGN's 8.8/10 review of the first film and our 5/10 review of the second.

articles.title: Netflix Tried to Bring Obsession Straight to Streaming Before It Exploded in Theaters
articles.summary: Director Curry Barker said Netflix bid to put Obsession straight to streaming before Focus Features helped it become the biggest box office success story of 2026.
articles.body:
Director Curry Barker said Netflix bid to put Obsession straight to streaming before Focus Features helped it become the biggest box office success story of 2026.

The comedian-turned-horror-filmmaker talked about the early days of his record-breaking low-budget flick during a conversation on Q with Tom Power . We all know how Obsession turned out, but Barker said offers for the project nearly kept it out of theaters for a very different life as a streaming exclusive.

Barker said an early screening almost immediately resulted in "everybody" putting in offers to distribute Obsession. Neon, Focus, A24, and more wanted to bring Barker's twisted monkey's paw tale under their banner. Focus eventually won the war, but not before Netflix offered to throw a wrench into things.

"All of these companies are wanting to do your movie," Barker recalled hearing from his manager. "At this time, I'm still thinking maybe small theatrical release. Maybe they just want to acquire it, and also, as a director, I'm thinking, I'm scared of, 'Are they going to want to change my movie? Are they going to want to take out certain parts that I like?'

"So many questions were being thrown around. I think Netflix was in the conversation at one point. They put in an offer to just put it straight on Netflix. All of these conversations started."

With the odd exception , Netflix has infamously strayed from theatrical releases in the past. Before Paramount swooped in to acquire Warner Bros., the streaming giant was reportedly only interested in keeping its new slate of films in theaters for a little more than two weeks . Its movie boss, Dan Lin, said in June that the company "just won't work with" filmmakers who push to bring their films to theaters .

All signs point to a streaming-exclusive release for Obsession should Barker have signed with Netflix – but we all know that's not what happened. Instead, audiences spent months swarming movie theaters to see how stars Inde Navarrette, Michael Johnston, Cooper Tomlinson, and Megan Lawless helped bring the director's vision to life. It brought home massive early returns at the box office on its notably low $750,000 budget and then continued to surprise before reaching an unbelievable global total of $519.4 million (via Box Office Mojo ).

It was an unprecedented run that almost didn't happen if Netflix had proved victorious. There's no telling if Obsession would have had the same impact if it remained available to stream from the start, but Barker and company are probably happy enough with how things turned out. Although he and Tomlinson are still working on getting their next feature, Anything But Ghosts, ready for release, the director does have some ideas for a sequel in mind, even if it will be a while before Obsession 2 gets off the ground .

For more, you can read what Barker had to say about Gen Z's opinions on "slop" in movies . You can also check out how Universal brought Navarrette's Nikki to Halloween Horror Nights and then see IGN's top-reviewed horror movies of the year . Obsession, for example, earned an 8/10 .

articles.title: Avengers: Endgame Encore Collects $86 Million in Theaters as New Scenes Help MCU Fans Prep for Doomsday
articles.summary: Avengers: Endgame Encore dusted off an estimated $86 million at the box office as new scenes helped bring MCU fans back to theaters to prep for Doomsday.
articles.body:
Avengers: Endgame Encore dusted off an estimated $86 million at the box office as new scenes helped bring Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) fans back to theaters to prep for Doomsday.

It's a gargantuan opening weekend for Disney and Marvel's Infinity Saga-ending re-release that saw it rank atop global charts. Of its $86 million debut, it earned $26 million domestically and $60 million internationally.

For those unaware of why Avengers: Endgame is back in theaters, there are a few reasons audiences have shown up in droves to watch the seven-year-old MCU movie. First and foremost, the Encore re-release comes with a few minutes of extra footage that ties directly into this December's superhero crossover event film, Avengers: Doomsday . With director Joe Russo previously setting up the new clips as "critical" to the next movie's plot , it seemed inevitable that at least die-hard fans would show up.

There's been plenty of debate about whether those new precious minutes of MCU footage could justify the price of another ticket , but with another $86 million in the bank, it seems there were plenty who thought it was enough. It helped that, outside of one scene , most of Avengers: Endgame Encore keeps the original story intact, giving moviegoers a chance to relive all of the hype moments and big reveals before Robert Downey Jr., Chris Evans, Chris Hemsworth, and more return to the MCU later this year.

As Avengers: Endgame Encore brings the end of Thanos' mission to conquer the universe with the Infinity Stones back to theaters, it also sees the return of one of the biggest theatrical releases of all time. The Avengers movie shattered records upon its release in 2019 and eventually returned later that same year for its first re-release . Many of its notable feats have held up in the seven years since, with only Tom Holland's Spider-Man: Brand New Day able to topple some of them last month.

Through it all, Avengers: Endgame has now soared to an unbelievable $2.885 billion worldwide total. Disney has marked it as the second-highest debut for a re-release ever, falling only behind 2012's Titanic 3D.

27 Awesome MCU Callbacks in Avengers: Endgame

While Marvel and Disney take what feels like an endless run of victory laps, Zach Cregger's Resident Evil proved it has some staying power after its second weekend in theaters. It brought in another $23 million domestically and $27 million internationally for a worldwide, with its two-weekend total sitting at $196.5 million on a reported $75 million budget. Despite facing an uphill battle with some fans , the Capcom video game-turned-horror-movie quickly became the highest-rated game adaptation of all time .

Also opening at the box office this weekend was the Brad Pitt-led and doggy-driven survival flick, Heart of the Beast , which brought $50.1 million globally and fetched an 8/10 review from IGN. Director Lance Oppenheim and star Robert Pattinson's Primetime , a big biopic based on Chris Hansen's To Catch a Predator that IGN awarded a 9/10 , earned $20.06 million globally, with the vast majority of that ($19.2 million) brought in domestically.

The top five films for the global box office from this past weekend saw Avengers: Endgame Encore take first, Resident Evil take second, and Heart of the Beast take third. Primetime and Forgotten Island rounded out the list in fourth and fifth, respectively.

Avengers: Endgame Encore is mostly the same movie we saw in 2019, but that doesn't mean it hasn't spawned plenty to talk about as Doomsday approaches. One topic on fans' minds involves a new star-studded, pre-movie opener that asks fans to silence their phones .

articles.title: 'It Was Really Great and Really Emotional' — Anthony Mackie Remembers Chris Evans Showing Him the Avengers: Endgame Script Early to Reveal How He'd Become Captain America
articles.summary: Anthony Mackie said Chris Evans told him how he'd become Captain America by showing him the Avengers: Endgame script early.
articles.body:
Anthony Mackie said Chris Evans told him how he'd become Captain America by showing him the Avengers: Endgame script early.

The Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) mainstay and former Falcon actor recalled finding out how Sam Wilson would take over the mantle as part of a conversation with Cigar Aficionado (via Variety ). Instead of a behind-the-scenes celebration or public reveal, Mackie said he learned the details about his new role as the next Captain America during a private moment he and Evans shared during the early days of working on Avengers: Endgame.

"Chris Evans is somebody who I hold near and dear," he said. "We're at Chris' house, and because he's Captain America, he gets the [script] pages first. So he’s like, 'Yo, did you read the new scene?' I'm like, 'Nah, what's up?' So, he takes me down…and he gave me the script and let me read it.

"And it was really great and really emotional to learn it from a friend…I don’t know a lot of actors who would have appreciated or celebrated that moment with a fellow actor in that way because I was taking his job for all intents and purposes."

The end of Evans' time as Captain America marked the conclusion of an eight-year arc that saw his Steve Rogers appear in three standalone films, multiple team-up movies, a few fun cameos, and more. He quickly cemented himself as the most recognizable incarnation of the character and delivered fan-favorite stories that are still celebrated as some of the best the MCU has to offer today.

To say Evans stepping away as Captain America represented a gargantuan shift for the MCU is an understatement. Mackie adopted the role in the closing moments of Avengers: Endgame in a scene that saw an aged Steve Rogers handing over his iconic shield, but the actor says his friendship with Evans meant he knew how he'd fill the role long before the rest of the world – and, it seems, much of the cast and crew.

Mackie went on to play the Sam Wilson version of Captain America in The Falcon and the Winter Soldier Disney+ show. His first standalone outing as the Marvel superhero was last year's Captain America: Brave New World .

Audiences will see him – and even Evans' Steve Rogers – return to the MCU when Avengers: Doomsday premieres December 18, 2026. MCU fans who hit theaters to see Avengers: Endgame Encore this past weekend got a sneak peek at what's in store thanks to a small collection of new scenes .

articles.title: Out of the Park Baseball lets me enjoy baseball even when the Mets suck
articles.summary: OOTP Baseball is a nitty gritty hyper-realistic baseball sim that puts you in the GMs office.
articles.body: If you were to ask me what game or game series I’ve sunk the most time into, the answer would be easy: Out of the Park Baseball (OOTP). I have spent roughly 2,300 hours, according to Steam, playing various editions of the game. OOTP isn’t like MLB The Show or Super Mega Baseball. It’s not graphically impressive. It’s not a blast of simple arcade fun. It is basically a spreadsheet pretending to be a video game. It’s fantasy baseball, but without having to wait six months to see how disappointing that sleeper draft pick will be, because you can plow through an entire season in as little as a few hours. You can play individual games and dig into play-by-play managing in OOTP if you want. But that becomes tedious. And frankly, it’s not where the game is the most fun. Instead, I think the game is at its best when you sit in the GM’s chair and maybe make some helpful “suggestions” about how to structure the lineup or bullpen. The UI is complicated and dense. 90 percent of the time, you’re just looking at rows of stats and scouting reports. And the level of detail is deep. OOTP includes not just current MLB players, but historical MLB players, all minor league teams, Korea’s KBO League, and even the entire World Baseball Classic. There’s something thrilling about digging through all this info and trying to find that diamond in the rough during a draft. Someone who might become the new franchise player for your favorite team in this alternate universe. Deciding whether to bet on that prospect developing into a superstar, or to trade them for an undeniable big-league All-Star is stressful. And you even have to worry about fans abandoning you if you fail to re-sign your favorite player. [Media: On my Mets, Brandon Nimmo isn’t just a good player, he’s a damned superstar. Kodai Senga has won three Cy Young Awards. I signed Juan Soto, but also traded a raft of mid-tier prospects for Ronald Acuña Jr., made the playoffs four years in a row, and eventually won a World Series. (Look, as a Mets fan, I need this fantasy world, don’t harsh my vibe.) Perhaps the best part of OOTP Baseball, though, is that it kinda lets you play however you want. It’s deeply customizable. You can manually play every game if you want. Or you can speed-simulate entire seasons in a couple of hours. Want an easier experience where players don’t get hurt? Turn down or off injuries. Don’t want to worry about budgets? Play in commissioner mode and tell the team owner where to stick it. And because it mostly just sits there, statically waiting for you, it’s easy to just leave it running in the background and dip in and out when you’ve got a few spare minutes. OOTP Baseball is a cozy sim for a very particular brand of sports nerd. If you love fantasy baseball and wish you could play it year-round (and don’t want to deal with friends arguing about whether their bid for Alonso came in on time), or maybe you dig the idea of a cozy game like Tiny Bookshop, but wish they had a more Sabermetric bent, OOTP Baseball might be for you. The current version, OOTP Baseball 27, is available now on Steam or directly from the developer.

articles.title: HBO's Lanterns Bounces Back in Episode 7 as Kyle Chandler's Hal Jordan Fully Returns to the Spotlight
articles.summary: Lanterns regains its lost momentum in Episode 7, as the show reconnects with the core Hal/John dynamic we love so much. Read our full review.
articles.body:
Warning: This review contains full spoilers for Lanterns Season 1, Episode 7!

The worst part about Lanterns finally diving into the 2026 storyline first teased back in the pilot is that it forces us into a post-Hal Jordan reality. So much of the appeal of the series rests on the sour dynamic between Kyle Chandler's Hal and Aaron Pierre's John Stewart, and there's just something missing without the former in play. Thankfully, there's a workaround in the form of the Halogram backup. Episode 7 exploits that loophole for all its worth, resulting in a new installment that digs far deeper into Hal's troubled psyche and dark family legacy.

Fittingly, this week kicks off with a flashback to Hal's childhood, where we finally meet Martin Jordan (Jake B. Miller) in the flesh. That opening sequence offers some valuable insight into Hal's character. We can see how Martin casually fostered the same sort of fearlessness in his son that the Stewarts mercilessly drilled into John. And we also get a taste of the deep-seated, suicidal depression that is clearly a generational legacy in Hal's family. Miller really shines in his brief time in the spotlight, expertly conveying Martin's bravado and pain in equal measure. And I have to assume the Sinestro-esque mustache is intentional, a subtle reminder of how much the orphaned Hal would come to look to his GL mentor as a father figure.

From there, things shift back to 2026, as the Halogram reacts to being dug up and reactivated after another 10-year hiatus. Again, the series makes the most of its ability to work around Hal's murder. We get that all-important Hal/John banter back, but with the twist that comes from having a slightly younger and less mean-spirited version of Hal in the mix. It's endlessly entertaining to watch the two interact and for the Halogram to convey some of the things his flesh-and-blood self could never admit.

We're also treated to a terrific scene involving Sheriff Kerry (Kelly Macdonald) reuniting with "Hal," one that features arguably Macdonald's strongest performance in the series to date. I'm not prepared to discount the theory that she was Hal's killer just yet (particularly if it somehow involved her protecting her son), but her grief is clearly genuine regardless.

"The Jordan Boys Legacy" does share one flaw with Episode 6. The drama involving the other Rushville locals just isn't that compelling. Granted, this episode doesn't suffer nearly as much in that regard because it's so much more focused on Hal and John's investigation, but there are still a few scenes focused on these less compelling subplots. I really can't bring myself to care about the blackmail conflict between John and Maggie (Hannah Christine Shetler). So he's out $315,000 and a fancy Richard Mille watch. Why does any of that matter in the grander scheme of John's Green Lantern origin story?

It's also tough to know what to make of the Noah (Shea Pritchard) of it all. On the surface, his little Hat Day runaround isn't that compelling, either. But there's obviously something deeper at work with the character. I fully suspect we'll learn in the finale that he's some sort of human/Manhunter hybrid and is at the heart of Hal's murder (assuming Hal is even dead, which we really can't ). I'm just glad the series is running out of room to prolong that particular mystery.

Finally, Episode 7 ends with John stepping foot onto an alien world for the first time. We quickly discover that Hal bequeathed a portal to Antaan's (Paul Ben-Victor) home planet, offering a glimpse of the devastation Manhunters can wreak. It's a nice change of pace seeing a setting other than Earth, even if the flat, featureless desert doesn't make for the most memorable view. It's more Stephanie Economou's eerie, discordant score that makes this setting feel hostile and otherwordly.

After a tense fear gas sequence and some more heart-to-heart moments between Hal and John, we're treated to a proper payoff to the entire sequence with the long-overdue return of Ulrich Thomsen's Sinestro. Naturally, him being marooned on a dead world instead of locked away on Oa raises more questions than it answers, but it's enough simply to see the character again. I just hope Episode 8 has enough room to address these many lingering questions and still wrap up John's season-long arc in a satisfying way. There's still a lot of ground left to cover.

articles.title: Castlevania's Iconic Soundtrack Gets Its Own Symphony, Brought to Life by a 25-Piece Power Rock Orchestra
articles.summary: Konami is celebrating Castlevania’s 40th birthday with a special symphony made up of a 25-member rock orchestra that will bring the series’ iconic sounds to fans in Tokyo, London, and Los Angeles.
articles.body:
Konami is celebrating Castlevania’s 40th birthday with a special symphony that will bring the series’ iconic sounds to fans in Tokyo, London, and Los Angeles.

Fans of the classic game series can expect a tour of its soundtracks all the way from the very first Castlevania title through the modern era, featuring the first-ever live performance of music from the upcoming Castlevania: Belmont's Curse .

This symphony, comprised of a 25-piece power rock orchestra, was created by Lambert Jackson productions, and features all-new arrangements and orchestrations from composer Adam Hoskins, the mind behind the viral Undertale : The Determination Symphony World Tour.

Konami confirmed that a few specific tracks will be featured in the show, including Bloody Tears, Vampire Killer, Divine Bloodlines, and Dracula's Castle from Symphony of the Night.

This orchestral concert will take place across three dates in March 2027, which we’ve listed below:

13 March: Tokyo Opera City Concert Hall, Tokyo

Tickets can be purchased on the event's official website . Tickets for the Los Angeles showing go on sale October 1 at 10 AM PT. Tickets for the London showing go on sale October 1 at 12 PM BST. The pre-sale tickets for the Tokyo showing are lottery-based, and will begin on October 1 at 12 PM JST. General ticket sales for the Tokyo show will go live at a later date.

If you’re familiar with the Castlevania games, you know this symphony is gonna rock. Castlevania famously boasts a signature musical style that has stayed with the games ever since the very first title released in the 80s; popularized by composer Michiru Yamane in Symphony of the Night, Castlevania is known for its fabulous symphonic rock soundtrack and ripping melodies that set it apart from any other franchise in the industry.

This concert is officially licensed by Konami, and it's one of the only Castlevania concerts to get the publisher’s blessing. However, if you’re keen on hearing some of these sounds live to get in the mood for spooky season, you can check out this fabulous 2019 show from the Youth Stockholm Philharmonic Orchestra , who performed nearly two hours’ worth of the series’ songs with a special performance from Michiru Yamane, herself!

Fans can also look forward to the next game in the Castlevania series, Belmont's Curse, which releases on October 15, 2026. You can check out our preview here , and read about more Castlevania games here .

articles.title: The Mummy 4 Set Photos Reveal Rachel Weisz as Evelyn O'Connell, Suggest Time Period
articles.summary: Set photos have revealed Rachel Weisz reprising her role as Evelyn O'Connell in the upcoming The Mummy movie.
articles.body:
Set photos have revealed Rachel Weisz reprising her role as Evelyn O'Connell in the upcoming The Mummy movie .

As reported by the Daily Mail , the 56-year-old actress was spotted in costume as librarian, Egyptologist, and action heroine Evelyn O'Connell in London. Specifically, the scenes were filmed outside the British Museum, and will reportedly appear early in the movie.

Weisz stars in the new The Mummy alongside Brendan Fraser nearly 20 years after the last The Mummy movie, 2008’s Tomb of the Dragon Emperor, came out. Weisz didn't appear in that divisive third entry (Maria Bello played the character instead). In March, director duo Matt Bettinelli-Olpin and Tyler Gillett suggested Tomb of the Dragon isn't considered canon .

Last year, Fraser, who plays Rick O'Connell, pointed to the power of stunt men ahead of filming . The 57-year-old sustained multiple injuries during the filming of The Mummy movies, including a torn spinal disc and a cracked rib, which led to numerous surgeries over several years. These injuries and surgeries took a significant toll on his health, and played a part in the actor taking a long break from his career.

Meanwhile, John Hannah will reprise his role as Jonathan Carnahan, the unscrupulous brother of Evelyn O'Connell. Hannah appeared in the first three Mummy movies. Elsewhere, Oded Fehr returns as Ardeth Bay .

Reaction to the set photos has been extremely positive, with fans praising Weisz's period-appropriate attire. The Mummy is set in 1926, The Mummy Returns in 1933, and Tomb of the Dragon Emperor in 1946. It's unclear when exactly The Mummy 4 is set, but it looks like it will be 1950s post-war London. In one of the set photos, Weisz holds what looks like a transistor radio, which were introduced in the mid-to-late '50s.

There’s still much we don’t know about The Mummy 4 — even its final title is unannounced. Last November, Fraser told the Associated Press he’d been waiting 20 years for the call to make another The Mummy, adding: “It’s time to give the fans what they want.”

The Mummy 4 hits theaters October 15, 2027.

articles.title: Where to Preorder Magic: The Gathering’s Reality Fracture Expansion (Out This Week!)
articles.summary: Magic: The Gathering Reality Fracture launches this week. Here's our updated guide on where to preorder Play Boosters, Commander precons, Bundles, and sold-out Collector Boosters.
articles.body:
Magic: The Gathering's Reality Fracture set launches this week, and despite the fact that we're leaving Middle-Earth behind and have Star Trek yet to come , this feels like the most exciting Magic set on the horizon — Universes Beyond or Universes Within.

MTG Reality Fracture is Selling Out Fast

The set sees Jace Beleren reshaping the multiverse to what he feels it should be, twisting new versions of iconic characters and cards in the process. There are also some neat lore implications to this "Echoverse", including Strixhaven's schools being twisted into Hexhaven versions.

The set arrived in prerelease this weekend (September 26-27), with full launch just days away on October 2. Here's what you can preorder, and what's included.

Notably, Amazon is currently out of stock of everything Reality Fracture, so you may have to look elsewhere, like Walmart, Target, Best Buy, or resellers at TCGplayer, to find boosters or sealed boxes in stock.

Building out your collection is easiest with Play Boosters, and you can preorder a box at Amazon for $164.70 .

This includes 30 packs, with Wizards of the Coast promising 60+ legendary cards per box. There are 14 cards per pack, so you’re getting a total of 420 in a box.

Looking for a series of boosters without buying a whole box? The bundle is worth a look. These include 9 Play Boosters, a promo card, and full-art lands.

You’ll also find a storage box and a spindown die, all up for preorder at $57.99 . Think of these a little like the "Fat Packs" of old.

Where to Find Sold-Out Reality Fracture Collector Boosters

At the time of writing, Collector Boosters for Reality Fracture are sadly all out of stock, unless you take a trip to a trusted marketplace like TCGplayer .

These have an MSRP of $26.99, making them much more expensive than Play Boosters, but this is where you’ll find the rarest cards in the set, as well as alternative art treatments.

Draft Night is becoming pretty popular in 2026, appearing a few times already this year, and this Reality Fracture version is the same concept.

The $89.99 box includes 12 Play Boosters to build a deck for up to four players, as well as 90 lands. The winner can claim a Collector Booster, which, as we’ve already mentioned, remains elusive.

Reality Fracture Feature First Four-Color Commander Deck in Years

For the first time in a long time, we’re getting a four-color Commander precon with the set dubbed Multiverse Reforged.

It’s helmed by Jace, but includes alternate reality versions of Magic creatures. You could preorder it for $49.99 , but that price is climbing closer to launch.

Part of that is due to the card list, which includes cool new versions of cards like Ob Nixilis, the Ascended, Omnath, Locus of the Void, and Avacyn, Angel of Horror. It also plays pretty well from early reviews!

For more on Magic: The Gathering, check out our guide to preordering the upcoming set based on The Hobbit , as well as our ranking of Secrets of Strixhaven’s Commander precons .

articles.title: 78-Year-Old Fortnite Streaming Grandmother Now Holds a World Record
articles.summary: Cath Bowie, a 78-year-old grandmother, now holds a world record for Fortnite streaming.
articles.body:
Cath Bowie, a 78-year-old grandmother, now holds a world record for Fortnite streaming.

The Scottish septuagenarian — better known online as Grumpygran1948 — has been officially decreed as the world's oldest Fortnite streamer (female) by Guinness World Records. Bowie began playing Fortnite in 2017, during the battle royale mode's launch week, making her a true OG.

Speaking to BBC News , the gaming grandma said she had been introduced to the game by her teenage grandson, who initially told her that nobody would watch a grandmother playing Fortnite — something she then took as a challenge.

"He just couldn't believe that his grandma would do such a thing and suggested that nobody would join me or watch me," Bowie said. "Saying that was like a red rag to a bull to me. I would show him that I could do it.

"Twenty four thousand followers later and he doesn't mention it," she continued. "I wonder why?"

Now, Bowie plays with others from across the world, and streams daily via YouTube and Twitch. Her achievement has also now been recognized by Fortnite developer Epic Games, which has described her as a "goat."

"You're trying to get the better of your opponents and eliminate them," Bowie said of Fortnite's main battle royale mode, which she appears to play in the popular Zero Build mode. "But there's no blood on the scene - you just shoot somebody and they either crawl about until they die or they're just obliterated with the one shot. So there isn't any mess — nothing like that."

articles.title: Fortnite Five Nights at Freddy's Announcement is Now the Game's Most Liked Reveal Ever, Beating the Avengers and Dragon Ball Z
articles.summary: Epic Games' announcement of a Fortnite and Five Nights at Freddy's crossover has now become the battle royale's most-liked post of all time on social media.
articles.body:
Epic Games' announcement of a Fortnite and Five Nights at Freddy's crossover has now become the battle royale's most-liked post of all time on social media.

Characters from Scott Cawthon's hit horror series will join Fortnite next month, in time for its annual Halloween shenanigans. Among FNAF fans, the excitement is definitely real — and enough to dethrone the confirmation of similar crossovers with all other major franchises.

At the time of writing, Epic Games' confirmation of FNAF has more than 312,000 likes, making it the account's most-liked post ever: more than Dragon Ball Z (282,000 likes), Naruto (214,000 likes), and Avengers: Infinity War (212,000 likes, all the way back in 2018).

The post has even been liked more than Epic Games' own reveal it would be bringing back the game's original map for an "OG" mode (216,000 likes).

A trailer for the collaboration appears to confirm that Freddy, Chica, Bonnie and Foxy will all gain Fortnite skins, alongside various other cosmetic items. A Five Nights at Freddy's in-game location will also be featured — and indeed, this pizza restaurant can already be found being built on the battle royale's Island map, acting as a teaser for the collaboration.

FNAF has long been one of the most fan-requested Fortnite crossovers, with hopes, dreams and plenty of memes anticipating its eventual arrival over the years. Originally launched in 2014, FNAF has expanded from a simple Steam game into a major franchise, with numerous sequels, spinoffs, novels and two major Hollywood movies.

If you'd like to go hands-on with Freddy in Fortnite for yourself, the skins are expected to launch later this week on October 1, when the annual Fortnitemares celebration kicks off. This is set to run longer than usual — for a full month, and essentially until the end of this year's Fortnite chapter. Fans then expect another mini-season to take place, similar to last year's beloved Simpsons takeover (top bets this year include a similar One Piece event.) After that, Fortnite is expected to relaunch yet again with its Chapter 8 incarnation, likely around the start of December.

articles.summary: Pokémon cards will return to McDonald's Happy Meals soon, with 15 more cards to collect.
articles.body:
Pokémon cards will return to McDonald's Happy Meals soon, with 15 more cards to collect.

According to PokéBeach , branches of McDonald's in the U.S. will feature packs of cards in Happy Meals from November 5 to December 9 this year, meaning you have just a month to collect them all.

As with previous versions of this hugely-popular promotion, 15 cards will be on offer via individual four-card booster packs, each of which will feature three regular cards and one holo.

If you recall, last year's Japanese promotion resulted in mass scenes of food waste, with uneaten burgers dumped in the streets, as fans and scalpers hunted for the card, and others. The retail chain then promptly ended the giveaways early and introduced tighter rules to clamp down on Pokémon scalping for future promotions .

articles.title: WoW Forever Beta Player Dies to a Near Perfect Griefing Tactic That I'm Sure Blizzard Will Patch Out
articles.summary: World of Warcraft Forever’s beta marches on, and all evidence points to it being a massive success. But it’s worth remembering this is a beta, and a beta is for reporting issues. Enter one of the best WoW griefing tactics I’ve ever seen.
articles.body:
World of Warcraft Forever’s beta marches on, and all evidence points to it being a massive success ahead of the official release date next month. But it’s worth remembering this is a beta, and a beta is for players testing the game's boundaries and developer Blizzard reacting when those boundaries are broken.

Enter one of the best World of Warcraft griefing tactics I’ve seen in Forever so far.

Player jamesja12 took to the WoW Forever subreddit to post a screenshot of their death. That would be nothing worth writing home about under normal circumstances — you die all the time in World of Warcraft. But this was a screenshot of their character after they had died during the intro cinematic, because one cheeky player had placed a campfire exactly where new players spawn.

For the uninitiated, when you create a character in World of Warcraft — and World of Warcraft Forever — you get a snazzy intro cinematic that sets up the part of the world you start in, as well as your role within it. The camera does a fly-by of the local area before resting behind your freshly spawned character, ready to set out adventuring.

In WoW Forever you can craft and place campfires, which are — normally — all about helping other players out. Sit next to a campfire and you’ll receive a useful buff and maybe strike up a conversation with another player doing the same. Campfires are really cool social tools, as well as great buffing machines. I like campfires!

But they also cause a little damage because, well, they’re fire. If you run through a campfire, for example, you’ll take damage, as most WoW players will know well. Pop a campfire down where new characters spawn and they’ll strip that low HP away pretty quickly.

“Someone made a campfire where new players spawn. It killed me during the intro cinematic,” jamesja12 said, matter of factly, while posting a screenshot of the evidence of the crime scene. Pretty annoying? Well, most of the reaction is from players who are pretty impressed by this griefing tactic, rather than outraged.

“This is diabolical. I love it, although it's pretty mean,” one player said. “My orc was grunting during the intro and I had no idea why lol,” jamesja12 replied, referring to the noise characters make when they take damage.

“Brings new meaning to the term ‘spawn camping,’” another player said. “I can’t even be mad at that,” added another. “This is peak classic wow, amazing,” commented another.

This is World of Warcraft, so war between the Horde and the Alliance is part of the game. I was questing in Westfall last night as it was being raided by a high level Horde player who was killing quest-giving NPCs. Some were complaining in the chat, others saying this is part of the game. These are 20-year-old debates, rekindled once again in WoW Forever, and it’s great fun to see.

But this is orc-on-orc griefing, so perhaps Blizzard will take a dim view of it. I expect the developer will patch it out in some way — especially after this reddit post blew up (6,000 upvotes and counting!). I totally respect the effort to grief here. Yes, it’s annoying, but this is a beta after all. Best not to get too upset about anything. Now, if this becomes a widespread issue when Forever launches proper next month, that’s another thing. But for now… well done everyone! Jamesja12 indicated they used the in-game tool to report the “bug,” so it’s probably not long for this world. Enjoy it while it lasts.

The WoW Forever beta was inundated with players , and Blizzard has suggested its popularity took even the developers by surprise. It’s had to increase the beta population cap multiple times already. Yeah, this is going to be a big one.

articles.title: CD Projekt Releases Official List of All the Improvements in The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered
articles.summary: CD Projekt has released an official list of all the improvements made for The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered.
articles.body:
CD Projekt has released an official list of all the improvements made for The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered .

The developer issued media with the updated list, which breaks the improvements down into four categories: visual, combat, quality of life, and miscellaneous. We’ve reproduced them below so you know what to expect when the game launches tomorrow, September 29.

We’ve also got the official The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered global release times , so you know when the game unlocks in your region, as well as the update download sizes so you can best prepare.

The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered Screenshots

“A lot has changed in the gaming world since The Witcher 3 first launched,” CD Projekt said in its note to the media. “We’ve continued to develop and improve the game over the years, with the last major update bringing the title to next-gen consoles. Never before, however, have we introduced so many extensive, far-reaching changes at once — Remastered is the first release of its kind for The Witcher 3.

“These changes affect every aspect of the game, with particular attention to exploration and combat mechanics. We’ve significantly improved a wide range of gameplay elements. Some features, such as the skill tree, have even been entirely rebuilt to ensure the best possible experience for both new and returning players. Whether this is your first time visiting the Continent or a long-awaited return to the Path, The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered was created with you in mind.”

The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered improvements:

From the sun-drenched hills of Beauclair to the snow-capped mountains of Skellige, the Continent has never looked so stunning. The world of The Witcher 3 is now more detailed than ever thanks to a range of visual improvements, while modernized lighting lets every location truly shine.

Upgraded Visuals and Performance — Remastered brings new detail and depth to every corner of the Continent with changes such as improved textures for the environment, NPCs, and monsters, major enhancements to foliage, and reworked lighting, rendering, and ray tracing.

Path Tracing (PC Exclusive) — Combined with other visual enhancements of Remastered, Path Tracing creates the most visually stunning version of The Witcher 3 ever made.

PS5 Pro Support — PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) enables a smooth 60 frames per second with ray tracing turned on, offering remarkable Visuals.

Overhauled combat feels modern, engaging, and more responsive than ever, and the skill tree—the heart of every RPG — has been rebuilt to radically improve player experience.

Reimagined Skill System — Discover brand-new abilities and skills with an overhauled skill tree that modernizes character progression, offering deeper flexibility and greater impact on your playstyle.

Improved Combat — With revamped animations, brutal new finishers, and an adaptive camera, the action feels more dynamic, fluid, and kinetic than ever before.

Sign Refresh — All five witcher signs — Aard, Igni, Yrden, Quen, and Axii — have been refreshed with exciting new visual effects.

Enemy Behavior Enhancements — Formerly routine encounters with enemies like wolves and drowners feel much more immersive and reactive thanks to updated enemy behavior.

Revamped movement animations, more engaging exploration, and a range of other gameplay enhancements make every adventure even more immersive than before.

Overhauled Animations — New animations for Geralt and Roach bring additional dynamism to movement and traversal, which now feels more fluid and realistic.

Witcher Senses Rework — Geralt’s witcher senses have been reworked with not just cleaner visuals but increased immersion, as new clues are only revealed by focusing on the right elements.

Refreshed UI — An updated main menu provides quicker access to key features, while refreshed quest and tutorial notifications keep new information clear and concise.

Transmog — Transmogrification allows weapons and armor to take on a new look without sacrificing their stats, bringing even more freedom to character Customization.

As part of Remastered, we’ve also introduced a range of other additions to The Witcher 3 that are worth highlighting. While they don’t fall under any one specific aspect of the game, they still represent significant additions to the overall experience.

Expanded Photo Mode — Make memories and capture thrilling moments with a wide array of photo mode options, including new poses, camera controls, frames, filters, models, and more.

Mod.io Integration — Cross-platform mod support opens the game up to a wealth of custom content. From new quests, weapons, and equipment to balance changes and more, mods create an entirely unique Witcher 3 experience.

Bard’s Ballad — Bard’s Ballad is a new accessibility feature designed for players with cognitive limitations such as attention deficits or cognitive fatigue. It adjusts selected gameplay elements to better accommodate players’ needs, for example by introducing automatic self-healing.

As for the Nintendo Switch 2 version, CD Projekt pointed to motion controls, which let players cast witcher Signs, fire the crossbow, throw bombs, drink potions, and speed up or stop Roach. Gyro aiming "offers greater precision in combat," while mouse mode gives players another control option. The touchscreen can be used to navigate the map or game menus, and play Gwent.

The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt - Remastered is available as a free update on PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and Nintendo Switch 2 from September 29. To ease you into Geralt’s life on the road, check out the Things the Witcher 3 Doesn’t Tell You , plus IGN’s The Witcher 3 Walkthrough and The Witcher 3 Endings guide, which outlines all of the major quests and choices in the base game and expansions (now bundled in with the Remastered edition). When you’re ready for the tough choices, check out our The Witcher 3 Sex and Romance guide to see who Geralt can smooch and all the opportunities to do so. And to make Geralt as strong a monster hunter as possible, check out all the Witcher Gear Locations , Places of Power Locations , and even Gwent Card Locations .

articles.title: Get Jiro Is a Worthy New Addition to the Adult Swim Lineup and a Fitting Tribute to the Late Anthony Bourdain
articles.summary: The late Anthony Bourdain's creative legacy lives on in Get Jiro, a worthy new addition to the Adult Swim lineup.
articles.body:
This is a spoiler-free review of the first episode of Get Jiro, which premieres on Adult Swim on October 3 and HBO Max on October 4.

It's been close to a decade since Anthony Bourdain's passing, and the sting hasn't faded. Bourdain was such an interesting personality who brought a unique perspective to the worlds of food and travel. It only stands to reason that perspective would also translate to fiction writing. The graphic novel Get Jiro has now been adapted into an animated series on Adult Swim, and the series is well worth a watch for anyone who considers themselves a Bourdain fan.

Based on the graphic novels co-written by Bourdain and Joel Rose and illustrated by Langdon Foss and Alé Garza, Get Jiro is set in a vaguely post-apocalyptic version of Los Angeles where society has all but collapsed and chefs are now the true power players. The idea being that, as humanity turns inward and becomes ever more obsessed with virtual reality and online entertainment, food is now the only pleasure that can't be digitized. Amid this new world order, a humble sushi chef named Jiro (Brian Tee) embarks on a quest for vengeance.

Basically, Get Jiro takes the tropes of a straightforward revenge thriller and embellishes the whole package by submerging it in the culinary arena. What might have been an overly formulaic story were it to star mobsters and assassins becomes something far more weird and compelling when knife-wielding chefs instead take center stage. This world is strange, surreal, and more than a little cut from the Blade Runner cloth, and it works. It's a satire that doesn't feel too out of line with our actual reality.

The titular character anchors the first episode well. Tee's Jiro is extremely soft-spoken and taciturn, but we learn everything we need to through his actions and his behavior around his fellow chefs and food suppliers. He's a character whose talent for creating mouth-watering delicacies is matched only by his skill with a blade. Again, he's a character who might come across as a little too generic in a more traditional crime thriller/martial arts setting, but the food angle helps keep things fresh and exciting.

In fact, Get Jiro's first episode is often at its best when it simply lingers on the act of making food. There's a Miyazaki-esque emphasis on the rote tasks and silent motions that go into cooking. The show's animation style is solid in general (if a bit stiff in motion), but those quieter scenes are where it shines the most, and where Bourdain's own influence is most evident.

The pilot is also adept at introducing the show's other key players, including rival mafioso chefs voiced by Titus Welliver and Alison Pill. These antagonist characters are perhaps a bit too broadly rendered for their own good, but once again, the food angle does help to offset that a bit. And with the graphic novel being given a full 10-episode adaptation, there's ample room to flesh out these characetrs as Jiro's bloody quest unfolds.

articles.title: Minecraft Dungeons 2 Is a Shallow Sequel That Provides Some Peaceful Button Mashing With Friends, but Does Little to Stand Out
articles.summary: This shallow sequel provides some peaceful button mashing, but does little to stand out.
articles.body:
One of the reasons Minecraft is my favorite game of all time is how alluring its world of endless possibilities is, so it’s a little strange that the Minecraft Dungeons series seems to represent the exact opposite. Minecraft Dungeons 2 is a brief, forgettable ARPG that’s as thin as they come, from its barebones story to its shallow gameplay, and you can see almost all it has to offer in the span of an afternoon. Simple, easygoing action is kinda the whole point here, but while there’s nothing actively offensive about this humdrum adventure, there’s also very little worth getting excited about either. The good news is that the minor improvements this sequel makes over the original are quite welcome, including more customizable characters and the added ability to jump, plus the new realm of the Sift adds some fresh color and creatures to the Minecraft universe – so if you’re looking to spend a mindless night or two swinging swords with your friends, you could do a lot worse than this.

If you didn’t play the first one, Minecraft Dungeons 2 takes the pixelated items and goofy mobs from Minecraft and throws them into an extremely light (and noticeably less gory) version of Diablo. You’ll delve into dungeons, smack around swarms of monsters, and tackle big ol’ slobbery bosses while hoovering up as much loot as you can along the way. But where most ARPGs lean hard into dizzying skill trees and loot with so many different stats you need a degree in mathematics to comprehend them, Minecraft Dungeons strips away most of that in favor of a much simpler framework. That makes it both more approachable and, almost equally, less interesting. While this sequel expands on the ideas from the first in modest ways, like by increasing the armor slots you’ve got from one to four, it mostly maintains that stripped down buildcrafting philosophy.

The roughly seven-hour story has your unnamed hero squaring off against an evil cabal of Illagers who gain access to a new dimension, called the Sift, and… actually, look at that, I’ve just about covered it all. The cutscenes and conversations to be found here are basically just a vague outline of a story that sends you to and fro to kill things and save the world, and that’s about as deep as it ever gets. It’s not like I was expecting some kind of emotional drama from my “Minecraft meets Diablo” game, but like most things in this adventure, there’s still very little to it.

The action is thankfully more developed than the story, adding some key features to the mix that make battling through the blocky world more enjoyable. I had completely forgotten, for example, that the original didn’t have a jump button, and having one here adds some needed platforming and light puzzles to solve – plus it gives you access to a new jump attack so you can drop a ‘bow on these filthy adds. You also have more options for enchanting your weapons and armor with special effects (which you unlock by conquering dungeons and completing quests throughout the world) as well as new artifacts that offer passive buffs, like increased damage with ranged weapons. All of these things are a decent step up from the original, but the vast majority of the moment-to-moment gameplay remains largely unchanged, and smacking samey zombies and Illagers tends to run thin quite quickly.

The fact that buildcrafting is mostly left up to whichever odd equipment you happen to stumble upon, rather than a class-based system, also means you and your co-op teammates all play exactly the same way, and you rarely have control over how your build feels (at least until you near the endgame), since you’re largely at the mercy of the RNG gods. For example, I wanted to play a rogue-type class, but kept finding big ass swords and tank-like items, so I ended up serving as our crew’s defacto melee fighter despite my best efforts. Not that there’s much of a difference anyway, since every player has access to the exact same dodge skill, base speed, weapon options, etc. and you won’t find a shield to add blocking to your arsenal or anything like that.

The handful of equipment slots you’re given offer a few perks each, like increased DPS or added benefits from using healing items, or the ability to shoot fireworks that explode and deal damage to everything in the vicinity (which are good for ringing in the new year, too). You’ll also find a small arsenal of melee and ranged weapons with which to thwack creepers and skeletons, each with just a single attack pattern for you to spam. As you progress, you’ll be able to add some neat enchantments to give weapons and armor a new perk, like one that makes you move faster after you score a kill, or another that lets your ranged attacks penetrate through a target, but none of them do much to shake up the hollow hacking and slashing.

TieGuyTravis' Favorite Isometric Action Games

The best part of Minecraft Dungeons 2 is the new area called the Sift, a magical, soul-powered realm filled with goat things, poisonous water, and more teal landscapes than was previously thought possible with the science of our day. This isn’t a game with a whole lot of personality, and it often feels like it merely wears a thin Minecraft skin – but this new dimension is one of the few ways in which it branches out to do its own thing, and it mostly succeeds at being an interesting place to explore. It’s got some new creatures and a super distinct vibe, with souls floating everywhere and dancing automatons roaming about. Unfortunately, this isn’t the best showcase of the new realm, since you’re mostly just plowing through areas killing things, so it really just made me wish I could wander around it in regular Minecraft. But in a game with not a whole lot of exciting stuff going on, getting to explore this new slice of the Minecraft universe was definitely a highlight.

Once you’ve completed the story, you’ll unlock the equally thin endgame, which adds a new activity called Soul Storms. These events summon more deadly enemies for a chance at better loot, but there aren’t really any other activities to pursue where you’ll really need this better gear – at least not yet. Mojang has said it has plans to roll out additional endgame content after launch, which could make this activity worth grinding some day, but for now it feels mostly like more of the same monotonous chopping and dodging I’d already had enough of by the end of the story. The new equipment, which adds an additional perk to all the weapons and armor you find within this elite tier, is a decent prize at least, so even though I immediately felt like there wasn’t much for me to do with my new kit, there’s something about obtaining cool stuff that’s a worthy end in itself.

Beyond the Soul Storms, you’ll mostly roam around, complete any side quests you hadn’t gotten to yet, replay boss fights from the story, and conquer the numerous optional dungeons that can unlock some new enchantment options for your gear. That’s all fine, but it’s all the same button mashing that will have worn out its welcome by that point. My friends and I tried to find reasons to stick around, curious if the story was just a primer for a more deep, compelling endgame (as is often the case with ARPGs), but it seems like that just hasn’t been built yet.

articles.title: Lanterns Episode 8 Trailer Hints at What's to Come in Season Finale, Sparks a Number of Theories
articles.summary: HBO has released a trailer for Lanterns Episode 8, which teases a number of significant plot developments for the Season 1 finale.
articles.body:
HBO has released a trailer for Lanterns Episode 8, which teases a number of significant plot developments for the Season 1 finale.

Episode 7 left John Stewart and the Hal Jordan hologram confronting Sinestro on a strange planet. John and the Hal hologram are trying to work out who killed the real Hal Jordan, and it feels like we’re getting close to some sort of answer. But what does Sinestro have up his sleeve?

The teaser for Episode 8, below, shows Sinestro challenging John and the Lantern Corps' mantra about having no fear, insisting fear is incredibly powerful (well he would say that, wouldn’t he?). This appears to be part of a plot to resurrect Hal Jordan, last seen dug up from his grave by John. The trailer suggests this resurrection will actually come about via the alien cloning machine we saw earlier this season (that ring impressed upon the skin of Hal’s arm indicates the technology was used on him in some way).

But is this all a misdirection? I wouldn’t be surprised. Perhaps Hal created a clone of himself so he could fake his own death ( James Gunn recently hinted that there's more to Hal's death that we think ). And what does Guy Gardner’s return — confirmed by the teaser — have to do with all this? Whatever this plan to resurrect Hal Jordan involves, it seems to risk some catastrophe. Is this what Sinestro wants? Is this what John wants? Is this, even, what Hal wants?

“Don’t be afraid to be afraid,” Hal appears to tell John, casting doubt on everything John has shown to be important to him — at least on the outside — so far. We then see John look up to the sky. Is this a hint that he will finally use the power of the ring to fly?

Previous episodes have shown John to somehow be able to manifest constructs without actually wearing the ring himself. Indeed, in Episode 7, the Hal hologram seems amazed that John's able to do this. John has some special power within him, which I suspect will be fully unveiled in Episode 8. Perhaps he uses this power to save the day.

DC Universe: Every Upcoming Movie and TV Show

The teaser shows Hal fighting a fire in his own home. The trailer is edited to suggest this happens after Hal’s resurrection, but I think it is a scene showing the events before his death. We’re told everyone in town hated his guts, so perhaps someone threw a molotov cocktail through his window, and we’re seeing the consequences of that play out.

What about Noah, the highschool quarterback and wannabe president of the United States? Fans believe Noah will be revealed to be a Manhunter, and that Kerry has kept his true identity a secret all these years. Did she kill Hal because he found out and threatened to expose him? Did Noah kill Hal to protect himself?

And why did Hal keep a portal to a planet where Sinestro was hiding out in his “failsafe?” Why did he posthumously lead John there? What’s the connection here?

I’ve really enjoyed Lanterns, and it feels sad to say the season ends this Sunday. I’ve got so many questions going into Episode 8, I just hope some of them are answered — and we get news of Season 2.

While you wait to find out, check out our review of Lanterns Episode 7 .

articles.title: Steam's Must-Play Rhythm Games
articles.body:
Steam Hype helps demystify PC games by introducing newcomers to whole worlds of gaming with its Genre Intros . If you’re fresh to Steam or just looking to bulk up your wishlist, it answers all the questions you were too afraid to ask.

Case in point: Rhythm games. Many a gamer has gone wading into the deep sea of DJMax and gotten lost to a killer KPop beat. But where should you start? Here are 10 picks that start small and escalate all the way expert-only. Better still, aside from the inclusion of one VR game, you also won’t need anything beyond a basic mouse and keyboard to play.

Inspired by Nintendo's classic Rhythm Heaven series, this is a great place for rhythm game newbies to get a feel for the kind of action to come while still limiting itself to a single input. Bits & Bops is a collection of cute call-and-response challenges through an assortment of minigames, culminating in a longer, tougher 'remix' that combines everything you’ve learned into one.

Developer/Publisher: 7th Beat Games/Indienova

Another one-button game similar to Bits & Bops, but with a consistent medical theme wrapped in an ongoing story. It starts simply enough, requiring you to tap the button on every seventh beat, but quickly escalates to include three intersecting rhythms. Indeed, it does a lot of weird and cool stuff within its one-button format, and has a ton of community-made stages. It can get pretty tough but each stage throws in unique surprises so it always feels fresh.

Developer/Publisher: D-CELL GAMES/Playstack

Unbeatable is effectively two games in one. The first – and arguably more important part – is an FLCL-inspired anime rock-opera story following a band in a world where music is illegal, so go do some crimes. This story mode is relatively relaxed and a gentle introduction for arcade mode, which is where things get really tough. Even though you only have two buttons to press to keep in time, you won’t believe how challenging and fleshed-out it can get!

Released: September 26, 2025 (Early Access)

Developer/Publisher: BubbyTabby/SKY HOUR WORKS

Originally prototyped for the Playdate (the cute little indie handheld with the crank-handle controller), Beatblock is an excellent experiment in rhythm controls. Using the mouse or analogue stick, block incoming bullets and avoid bombs while clicking when the beat circle closes around you. But what really makes this one sing is that the levels feel like choreographed music videos with you at the centre of the action. Tons of user-created content on this one too, and it’s not even finished yet!

Developer/Publisher: Team Vividstasis/Hajimeli & SKY HOUR WORKS

This one might be a bit of a difficulty spike if you’re coming straight from Beatblock, so be ready to dial the difficulty down. This colossal four-button rhythm game has an extensive visual novel story mode, online multiplayer and much more, and it’s completely free. It features dozens of guest artists and crossovers with a load of other rhythm games, so the number of tracks it includes is in the hundred. Just don’t be ashamed to dial it down to Opening (Easy) mode.

DJMax Respect V is the latest in a long-running series which has been around since 2004. With support for between four- to eight-button play and hundreds of tracks across all kinds of genres, plus plenty of play-modes and fiercely competitive online ranking, this is a go-to for a reason. It doesn’t have user-created tracks here and DJMax can be very expensive – at full price, it’s close to $800! But hold out and you can often find it for much less.

Developer/Publisher: Vitamin Games/Kwalee

In Afterbeat (formerly Project Arrhythmia), you’re stuck in an animated music video where every part of the laser light show hurts . Less a typical rhythm game, more pacifist bullet hell where the music is the enemy, it comes with a powerful in-game editor to create your own stages you can share on Steam Workshop. And despite still being in early access, it already has thousands of user-made stages already.

A relatively recent Early Access debut but already extremely promising, Dead as Disco takes the stylish, choreographed fighting of the Batman: Arkham series – intercepting attacks, parrying and countering with effortless grace – and syncs it all to a beat. Every punch, kick, parry or block becomes part of the soundtrack, the crunchy impact noises becoming layers of percussion.

It would be remiss of us not to mention that rhythm games have found a big audience in VR, usually with calorie-burning benefits too. The uncontested king, favoured by casual and obsessives alike, is the block-slicing lightsaber rave king, Beat Saber. It’s available on almost all over VR platforms but is best on PC, thanks to an amazing modding scene that has elevated the game into whole new dimensions. Literally.

Developer/Publisher: Anarch Entertainment

Lastly, a game by rhythm game freaks for rhythm game freaks. Projekt Godhand bills itself as the "ULTIMATE TOOL ASSISTED BULLSHITTING KEYBOARD DESTRUCTION RHYTHM GAME", which means it’s an eight-button rhythm game with a love of high-BPM gabber nonsense. Interestingly it doesn't track which keys you're hitting, just which side of your keyboard, so you’ll find yourself slamming your hands frantically across the buttons to the beat. Just don't assume that because it's silly that it's easy; it just means the game doesn't have to play by anyone's rules anymore, only the beat matters.

Whether you’re a beginner or a master looking for your next musical obsession, we reckon that’s a good lineup to start with. But that’s just the abridged version. If you want the full details on all these games and a whole bunch more, check our our full-featured intro to rhythm games here , along with plenty more Genre Intros over on Steam Hype .
