articles.title: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered Update Patch Notes Include PC-Specific and Console-Specific Changes
articles.summary: CD Projekt has released the patch notes for The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered update, confirming PC and console-specific changes to the single-player role-playing game.
articles.body:
CD Projekt has released the patch notes for The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered update, confirming PC and console-specific changes to the single-player role-playing game.

Adding to its official list of improvements for The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered , CD Projekt has now released detailed patch notes that anyone downloading the update tomorrow will find interesting, as published on The Witcher website .

The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered releases September 29 on PC (Steam, GOG, Epic Games Store, Battle.net), PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and Nintendo Switch 2. If you bought any version of the game in the past, physical or digital, you can upgrade for free to the Remastered version within the same platform ecosystem as soon as it releases. (We’ve got the official The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered global release times , so you know when the game unlocks in your region, as well as the update download sizes so you can prepare.)

CD Projekt also issued a warning to fans that with the improvements introduced throughout The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered, the system requirements for the game have changed. The image below confirms the PC specs:

To ease you into Geralt’s life on the road, check out the Things the Witcher 3 Doesn’t Tell You , plus IGN’s The Witcher 3 Walkthrough and The Witcher 3 Endings guide, which outlines all of the major quests and choices in the base game and expansions (now bundled in with the Remastered edition). When you’re ready for the tough choices, check out our The Witcher 3 Sex and Romance guide to see who Geralt can smooch and all the opportunities to do so. And to make Geralt as strong a monster hunter as possible, check out all the Witcher Gear Locations , Places of Power Locations , and even Gwent Card Locations .

The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered update patch notes: Visual and Rendering

Updated multiple textures and models based on assets from The Witcher 3 HD Reworked Project .

Improved lighting and shading for grass and foliage.

Updated the visual effects of Signs, including their upgrade versions.

The game now features native DirectX 12 rendering with multithreading for better performance and visuals.

Updated tone mapping for improved colors, lighting, contrast and detail.

Added GTAO (Ground Truth Ambient Occlusion) as a new Screen Space Ambient Occlusion option.

Updated the HDR calibration panel by adding new options and other improvements.

Added Ray-Traced HairWorks for improved lighting and shading on hair.

Improved Motion Blur with a higher-quality, more cinematic look.

Updated Subsurface Scattering for more natural skin rendering.

Improved terrain and material rendering for more natural lighting, shadows, reflections, and highlights.

Implemented new Image-Based Lighting (IBL) for improved ambient lighting and reflections across different environments.

Reworked Bloom for more improved lighting effects across different environments.

The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered Screenshots

Improved the skill system. Skills are now organized into a skill tree and each skill has three ranks. Unlocking new skills now requires having the necessary prerequisite skills rather than spending a set number of skill points. IMPORTANT: As a result of these changes, your skill points have been reset.

Rebalanced the skill tree by refining skill bonus values, effects and synergies.

Renamed some skills to better reflect their effects.

You can now Reforge your equipment to change its appearance without affecting its stats. Only master craftsmen (Yoana and Hattori) offer this service. Unlock appearances by adding new equipment and crafting diagrams to your inventory. Dyes from Blood and Wine applied to equipment will carry over to the reforged item.

Polished the combat behavior of all non-boss monsters, including their attack patterns, counterattacks, movement, reactions, flight and the application of effects.

Cantering and galloping now requires pressing the button instead of holding it.

Added a new "Horse control input sensitivity" slider in Settings → Controls.

Improved Roach's and Geralt's movement, player control and animations: Refined Geralt's jumping animation so that it feels more natural and polished. Note: This doesn't affect jump distance and height. Added new finisher animations for Geralt. Added new idle animations for Geralt. Improved Geralt's ledge climbing, ladder climbing and vaulting animations as well as his speed for more responsive, fluid movement. Improved Geralt's gap closing animations in combat for smoother gameplay. Improved target-lock switching when moving the camera in combat. Polished animations for mounting and dismounting Roach, as well as cantering and galloping.

Refined Geralt's jumping animation so that it feels more natural and polished. Note: This doesn't affect jump distance and height.

Added new finisher animations for Geralt.

Improved Geralt's ledge climbing, ladder climbing and vaulting animations as well as his speed for more responsive, fluid movement.

Improved Geralt's gap closing animations in combat for smoother gameplay.

Improved target-lock switching when moving the camera in combat.

Polished animations for mounting and dismounting Roach, as well as cantering and galloping.

Meditation now features a timelapse instead of a UI screen for a more immersive feel.

The skill screen is now reorganized into a more intuitive skill tree layout.

Updated the map screen to make switching between tracked quests easier. Untracked quests now have a distinct marker and can be tracked by selecting it.

You can now hide herbs, boats and corpses on the minimap in Settings → Video → Interface for a cleaner, less distracting view.

Improved quest notifications by combining quest updates into a single HUD notification.

Nearby loot can now be grouped into a single window, so you no longer need to browse through multiple loot windows. You can enable this feature in Settings → Gameplay.

Added a loot feed that displays recently collected items on the left side of the screen. You can disable it in Settings → Gameplay.

Added item tooltips to the loot window, allowing you to preview an item's details before picking it up.

Renamed the "HUD Configuration" section in Settings to "Interface".

Updated the CD PROJEKT RED Account connection, My Rewards and telemetry consent menus.

Updated the Photo Mode UI and vastly expanded its features and options:

You can now choose from multiple different characters to place in your shot.

Added a selection of poses and expressions for Geralt and placeable characters.

Added a Look-at dropdown, allowing you to choose where Geralt and placeable characters direct their gaze.

You can now place lights and adjust their brightness, color, angles and more.

Added a confirmation prompt before exiting Photo Mode to help prevent accidental exits.

You can now lock the camera position in Photo Mode to make sure you capture the perfect shot.

Added the option to apply different environment presets to your scene.

Added the option to save camera presets, allowing you to save and reuse camera positions and angles.

You can now change the aspect ratio of your screenshot.

Added the option to toggle a first-person camera mode so you can see the world through Geralt's eyes.

You can now enable or disable camera collisions with objects and walls.

Set the perfect scene by changing the weather and time of day.

Adjust the intensity of weather effects like rain or storms.

Added an option to toggle Rule of Thirds lines in various aspect ratios, with optional cinematic black bars.

Camera coordinates will now be visible in the UI.

Added an option to hide surrounding NPCs.

Added placeable props, giving you even more ways to create the perfect scene. Just don't ask where they all came from.

The cursor is now visible in Photo Mode on PC when using a mouse.

Added a new Accessibility section to the Settings menu. Moved existing accessibility-related options there.

Added the Bard's Ballad preset. You can enable it when starting a new game on the Just the Story difficulty or during the game in the Accessibility section. It is designed to reduce cognitive load for players who experience mental fatigue or have difficulty concentrating. It streamlines gameplay by simplifying certain mechanics and disabling select features for a smoother, more focused adventure. You can enable the preset in the Accessibility tab and customize it by enabling or disabling the following options: Vitality Regeneration Boost - Gives the possibility to adjust its activation threshold ("Activates below (%) Vitality") and the rate at which Vitality increases ("Regeneration Intensity"). Infinite Breath - Geralt can't run out of oxygen while swimming and diving. Unlimited Item Durability - Your gear will never wear down, so there's no need to visit craftsmen for repairs. Unlimited Boat Durability - Boats are indestructible, making jagged rocks and sirens no longer a concern. Ignore Item Weight - Travel the Path carrying as much as you want. Faster Boats - Sail faster across the seas. The seas around Skellige just got a little bit smaller. Toggle Witcher Sense - Toggle on and off without having to hold the button.

Vitality Regeneration Boost - Gives the possibility to adjust its activation threshold ("Activates below (%) Vitality") and the rate at which Vitality increases ("Regeneration Intensity").

Unlimited Item Durability - Your gear will never wear down, so there's no need to visit craftsmen for repairs.

Unlimited Boat Durability - Boats are indestructible, making jagged rocks and sirens no longer a concern.

Ignore Item Weight - Travel the Path carrying as much as you want.

Faster Boats - Sail faster across the seas. The seas around Skellige just got a little bit smaller.

Toggle Witcher Sense - Toggle on and off without having to hold the button.

Streamlined tutorials to keep them concise and focused on teaching core game mechanics. We think Vesemir would approve.

Added an option to quickly disengage from combat. Hold the dodge button (Alt/〇/B) to unlock from your target, then press the sprint button (L Shift/X/A) to run away.

You can now collect loot without dismounting Roach.

Added Cross Platform Mod Support, an in-game tool powered by mod.io that allows you to easily browse and install player-created mods to customize your game. You can find it in the game's main menu in Mods. Log in with your CD PROJEKT RED Account, connect it to mod.io and start browsing. You can find more information about the Mod Manager here .

Various engine, UI and other improvements for REDkit, making it easier for modders to create, manage and customize their content.

Fixed an issue where it wasn't possible to change Right Stick Sensitivity if the settings were accessed directly from the main menu.

It's now possible to set Stick Sensitivity to the value of 0.69.

Fixed an issue where HDR settings would sometimes not appear on consoles.

In the Eternal Fire's Shadow - Fixed an issue where the Forgotten Wolf School Gear Diagrams weren't displayed in the UI after being received as a reward.

Wine is Sacred – Fixed an issue where fast traveling out of Toussaint during the "Search the wine cellar with Anna Henrietta" objective could block quest progression. This fix is not retroactive, so players who encountered this issue will need to load a save from before it occurred.

IMPORTANT: Make sure you have the latest graphics drivers installed. Grab them here: NVIDIA , AMD , Intel .

Added support for NVIDIA DLSS 4.5, together with Ray Reconstruction.

Added support for AMD FSR 4, including Frame Generation and Anti-Lag 2. FSR 4 is supported on AMD Radeon RX 7000 Series and newer graphics cards. On unsupported GPUs, the game will use FSR 2 instead.

Added support for Intel XeSS 2.0, together with Frame Generation and Low Latency.

Added support for DualSense controller haptic feedback.

If you've been holding off on picking up a Nintendo Switch 2, Argos has a particularly tempting bundle available as part of its Next Level Gaming sale . The retailer is currently selling the console with your choice of one of four Switch 2 games for £374.99.

The standard Nintendo Switch 2 is currently available for £354.99 at several UK retailers , so you're paying just £20 extra to add a game to your purchase. The bundle lets you choose from Cyberpunk 2077, Pokémon Pokopia, Metroid Prime 4: Beyond, and Star Fox, giving you a decent spread of options depending on what you're looking to play.

The £20 game offer is particularly appealing given that these are full-priced Switch 2 releases, rather than a throwaway pack-in game. If you were already planning to buy the console and one of these games, you're essentially getting the game at a significant discount as part of the bundle.

It's also worth noting that Argos has a few other console deals running as part of its Next Level Gaming sale , including a similar offer on PS5.

Argos is also offering a PS5 1TB console with Marvel's Wolverine for £589.99 , bringing the cost of the game down considerably compared to buying the two separately.

The PS5 normally costs £569.99, while Marvel's Wolverine is £59.99, putting the combined RRP at £629.98. With the bundle priced at £589.99, you're effectively getting Insomniac's latest Marvel game for £20 when you buy the console.

articles.title: Avengers: Endgame Encore Cinemagoers Issue Warning After Realizing Disney Locked Major New Scene Behind IMAX and Infinity Vision Theaters
articles.summary: Avengers: Endgame Encore viewers have issued a warning to fans after realizing Disney locked a major new scene behind IMAX and Infinity Vision theaters.
articles.body:
Avengers: Endgame Encore viewers have issued a warning to fans after realizing Disney locked a major new scene behind IMAX and Infinity Vision theaters .

The re-release of Marvel Studios' Infinity Saga conclusion made a splash in theaters in its opening weekend as moviegoers flocked to relive memorable hype moments and catch a glimpse of a few new Avengers: Doomsday teases. The new scenes, of which there are four in total , are arguably the biggest selling point of Avengers: Endgame Encore, so when some fans left the theater having only seen three, they were less than pleased.

"I just got back from a regular showing of Endgame Encore (2D screening) and I’m really frustrated that I didn’t get to see all the new footage," Reddit user Tyler_the_hourman said in a popular post they authored after they left the theater. "It was completely unknown to me (and the others in my showing) that we wouldn’t get the full cut with all the new footage.

This same fan admitted some may feel they got what they "paid for," but they say it "still feels so scummy." They clarified that they, like many others, tend to avoid social media ahead of new Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) releases so as to avoid any major spoilers. Avengers: Endgame Encore, despite being a spruced-up re-release, was no different, so they didn't learn about Disney's scene exclusivity strategy until it was too late.

The House of Mouse announced plans to lock new Doomsday teases behind IMAX and Infinity Vision screenings in late August. It was a relatively quiet announcement that, based on reactions online, didn't make it around to quite as many viewers as you might expect. There's also the fact that the reveal only promised that these exclusive scenes feature "an additional sneak peek," so no one truly knew what to expect until they walked into theaters September 25.

Warning! Avengers: Endgame Encore spoilers follow.

We now know that the four bonus sequences, which run for a combined total of around four minutes , feature an extended ending for Steve Rogers and Peggy Carter , a meeting between Bruce Banner and Doctor Doom, a fiasco at the TVA, and a few frames of what seems to show the forging of Victor von Doom's mask. It's the TVA scene, which looks like it may have been ripped straight out of Doomsday itself and features more than a few surprise cameos, that was left out of standard screenings.

Assemble respectfully. Silence your phones when you see Avengers: Doomsday, in theaters December 18. Get tickets now: pic.twitter.com/550mzSqS5w — Marvel Studios (@MarvelStudios) September 28, 2026

Assemble respectfully. Silence your phones when you see Avengers: Doomsday, in theaters December 18. Get tickets now: pic.twitter.com/550mzSqS5w

Loki series regulars like Mobius (Owen Wilson) and OB (Ke Huy Quan) show up for the extended look, which shows that not all is well with the Time Variance Authority as the multiverse begins to cave in on itself. It's maybe the longest scene of the four shown with Avengers: Endgame Encore, and it lives up to director Joe Russo's teasing . So, as fans are confused and frustrated to learn they missed out on one of the biggest Doomsday teases simply because they either don't live near a theater supporting IMAX or Infinity Vision screens or because they weren't willing to fork over the extra cash required for often pricier formats.

"It's a pretty scummy way Disney did this," one fan said . "Can't believe some people are actually defending this strategy of theirs."

"That's weird I thought the point of the rerelease was to add the new scenes," another said .

Hot Toys Avengers: Doomsday Victor von Doom Figure

"Cash grab" is a frequent phrase shared by MCU fans who are aware Disney kept certain scenes locked to premium theaters. Others are only just learning of the move now, as moviegoers leave their local theater and take to social media to express their frustration.

"I didn’t realize it until this post. IMAX Encore had even more footage than what I saw?" one Marvel fan said . "Interesting that they would partner with IMAX when all the IMAX theaters for Doomsday are taken by Dune."

"I literally just got back from seeing The Odyssey in IMAX and the trailer they screened for Endgame Encore said nothing about new footage being exclusive to IMAX," another Reddit user said .

"This is a shameless Disney cash grab," another reply added . "I'm not blowing all that money and driving out of my way to a Disney-owned theater just to go see five minutes of added footage. I'm sorry you got screwed."

Consider this story your PSA: If you want to see every new tease for Doomsday, you'll want to head to an IMAX theater when watching Avengers: Endgame Encore. It's currently unclear how long the re-release will stick around in theaters, but considering it made an impressive $86 million at the box office during its opening weekend, expect to see it hang around for at least a little while longer.

Avengers: Doomsday will follow up on all of the teases when its premiere marks the beginning of the end of the Multiverse Saga December 18, 2026. For more, you can read about how Anthony Mackie learned he'd be picking up Captain America's shield . You can also check out IGN's original 9.5/10 Avengers: Endgame review .

articles.title: 'We Did Circle It For a Long Time, That Idea': Avengers Directors Discuss Plans to Show Steve Rogers Returning the Infinity Stones
articles.summary: Avengers: Endgame and Doomsday directors Joe and Anthony Russo wanted to show Steve Rogers' journey to replace the Infinity Stones "for a long time."
articles.body:
Avengers: Endgame and Doomsday directors Joe and Anthony Russo wanted to show Steve Rogers' journey to replace the Infinity Stones "for a long time."

Rogers agrees to return the Infinity Stones to their places across the MCU timeline in the finale of Avengers: Endgame, before settling back in time to live out a happy life with Peggy Carter. (A life that will now be interrupted by the events of Avengers: Doomsday , it has been confirmed.)

While this journey hasn't yet been shown on screen, fans have long called for a Disney+ series featuring Chris Evans as he adventures across the Marvel timeline, dropping off various stones back where the Avengers found them. There's some fertile ground for exploration here too, as Evans could reunite with younger versions of his former team as well as former foes. It would be great to see Rogers bid a final goodbye to Black Widow before her later death, or face off once again with Red Skull.

Avengers: Doomsday Trailer: First Look at Doctor Doom

Clearly, the Russos also thought similar. Speaking to CBR , Joe Russo said that he and his brother Anthony Russo "did have that conversation," around showing Rogers' journey, before suggesting it would have been too difficult to show within a single film just as a montage.

"I think we toyed around with an idea of like, 'Is there a montage where he puts the stones back?' We felt like it just played past the ending," he explained. "We were like, 'It seems like much more complicated than a montage could sustain.' And so we didn't do it."

"We did circle it for a long time, that idea," Anthony Russo added, before seemingly discounting the idea of a Disney+ series. "I think that's a great idea," he continued. "How about a movie?"

This discussion is interesting as it appears to dovetail with comments made in the past by Evans himself, who said he had received numerous pitches to return to the MCU that he ultimately did not move forward with, as he waited for an idea big enough that justified going back.

While Marvel rarely discusses its discarded project ideas, it's not difficult to imagine a movie showing Steve's journey being pitched to Evans at some point. However, at present, there's no sign that this is a journey we'll ever actually get to see, as the Russos are busy enough still tinkering with Avengers: Doomsday, and entering pre-production on Avengers Secret Wars.

As for Doomsday, we know that it will pick up Steve's story after his Infinity Stone mission, as his life with Peggy Carter is disturbed by a visit from Loki. This is a moment that viewers have now seen play out in the extended version of Avengers: Endgame now playing in theaters . Exactly what happens after that, however, we'll need to wait a few months to see — when Avengers: Doomsday arrives December 18.

articles.title: Why Is Everyone Talking About LA Noire 2 All of a Sudden?
articles.summary: Rumors of an LA Noire 2 have been floating around, but is there actually any truth to them?
articles.body:
Rumors of an LA Noire 2 have been floating around the internet lately, but is there actually any truth to them?

Over the weekend, eagle-eyed fans dug up an old GTA 6 leak from 2023 . The leak originated on 4Chan and revealed a bunch of details that have actually since been confirmed. Perhaps one of the most notable bits is that Rockstar once planned to have four protagonists in GTA 6 , but eventually settled on two, which was recently confirmed by Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson. However, it is worth noting that this tidbit was also buried in a report from Axios a year prior to the 4Chan leak, as well.

The post went on to reveal details about the game's relationship mechanic, which has also since been confirmed, and teased some spoilers that have been loosely corroborated in other legitimate leaks in recent years. However, the reason people are digging this post back up is because it claims that Rockstar's next game is a sequel to LA Noire, set to release in 2030.

The game would be set in San Francisco and center around the Zodiac Killer, who terrorized the city in the '70s. If there ever were to be an LA Noire followup, this would be the most ideal story to tackle, given that it's rich with unique crimes, people, and has a great setting. So... is any of this real? Let's look at all of the evidence.

For starters, LA Noire was developed by the studio Team Bondi, led by a man named Brendan McNamara. Rockstar published the crime game and lent some developers to assist on the project. Unfortunately, Team Bondi dissolved shortly after LA Noire's release. Not long after, McNamara founded a new studio to make a successor known as The Whore of the Orient ( which we reported new details on earlier this summer ) without the help of Rockstar.

The game was scrapped due to funding issues and McNamara founded yet another studio known as Video Games Deluxe, which helped port LA Noire to VR devices. The studio was acquired by Rockstar in 2025 and renamed to Rockstar Australia, leading many to wonder what they're up to, exactly.

Presumably, they're helping with GTA 6, but a lot of the studio is comprised of ex-LA Noire creatives, including McNamara, who is a renowned storyteller. It seems hard to imagine that a creative like him would be relegated to leading a support studio, so it seems feasible that there could be plans for more games with him at the helm.

Rockstar has also shown an interest in the IP multiple times over the years. LA Noire was the second Rockstar game behind GTA 5 to be ported over to Xbox One and PS4, which raised eyebrows, given fans were more interested in titles like Bully, Red Dead Redemption, or even GTA 4. A condensed version of the game was also ported to VR around the same time, which was an unusual level of investment for Rockstar.

More recently, Take-Two Interactive CEO Strauss Zelnick was asked about the possibility of LA Noire returning . He noted that the door is open for Rockstar to revisit the game, so long as there's a team that's passionate about it.

“Broadly, we’re looking at doing something in the future with all of our intellectual property,” he said in April 2026. “There’s nothing to announce on LA Noire specifically, and if there were, it would be Rockstar announcing it, not me. But in any case, with regard to our legacy IP, the teams are always looking at what we have and we’re always thinking about it. The question is, at any given time, do we have a team that’s passionate about working on that?”

Whether McNamara is invested in another period crime drama remains to be seen, but his team would likely be the ones most gung-ho about going back to LA Noire. In 2012, Rockstar also teased that an LA Noire sequel wasn't off the table, as it was pleased with how the game performed, and Take-Two even noted its importance as a "franchise" moving forward.

"Don't count out the possibility of a new game in the LA Noire franchise in the future," said Rockstar during a fan Q&A. "We simply have not decided anything. We're all very pleased with how that game turned out and are considering what the future may hold for LA Noire as a series. We don't always rush to make sequels, but that does not mean we won't get to them eventually – see Max [Payne] and Red Dead for evidence of that – we have so many games we want to make and the issue is always one of bandwidth and timing."

Either way, it's an exciting prospect to consider, but there are a lot of questions over what direction Rockstar will take post-GTA 6. The game is expected to be the biggest entertainment launch in history, and the studio will likely support the hell out of it with updates over time, especially when its online mode launches in the future .

Will that be all-consuming, eliminating any chance of "smaller" games like an LA Noire sequel, or will the financial success afford Rockstar the opportunity to make more interesting artistic plays? We'll just have to wait and see, but Rockstar is already set to publish a pair of Max Payne remakes , developed by Remedy, so there are opportunities outside of heavily monetized online games.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: Spirit Halloween Has an Official Dungeon Crawler Carl Costume, but Here's How to Build Your Own
articles.body:
The Dungeon Crawler Carl books have really popped off this year. With the release of the eighth book in the series, the first graphic novel collection, and an official TV series announcement, there's a lot for Matt Dinniman fans to be excited about in 2026.

In addition to the actual story, there's been a ton of new Dungeon Crawler Carl merch available this year. And now that Halloween is approaching, there's even an officially licensed Carl costume at Spirit Halloween.

The Spirit Halloween is known to parody a lot of popular media with its costumes each year, but this version is actually officially licensed. So instead of being called something like "Dungeon Bomb Guy" or "Fantasy Boxer Shorts Man," the name is just simply "Dungeon Crawler Carl Costume."

The costume itself is actually pretty good and true to the Carl you'll find in the early books. It's got his classic heart boxer shorts, his enchanted gauntlet, and even a stick of dynamite to complete vibe. At $59.99, it's an easy out-of-the-box options for anyone looking to rep their favorite LitRPG book series this year.

The only problem with Spirit Halloween costumes, in my opinion, is that they are usually made of very flimsy materials. If you're looking for something that looks more legit, it's pretty easy to replicate this entire costume with higher-quality products or craft a DIY version with stuff you may already own.

Carl is a pretty simple character design, so a lot can be done with a little. If you're hoping to just buy all of the individual parts on Amazon, I've done most of the work for you here. In general though, here's everything you need for a base Carl costume:

Outside of those six key items, there are some things you can do to make it feel more like Dungeon Crawler Carl and less like a biker vagabond. articles.title: "As Far as I'm Concerned, That's a Step in the Right Direction" – Path of Exile Dev Optimistic About Diablo 5
articles.summary: While Diablo 5 was announced at Blizzcon 2026 just a couple weeks ago, the game doesn't come out until Spring 2029. But it seems like Chris Wilson, Ex-Co-Founder of Path of Exile developer Grinding Gear Games, is tentatively excited for Blizzard's next ARPG.
articles.body:
While Diablo 5 was announced at Blizzcon 2026 just a couple weeks ago, the game doesn't come out until Spring 2029. But it seems like Chris Wilson, former co-founder of Path of Exile developer Grinding Gear Games, is tentatively excited for Blizzard's next ARPG.

Wilson, who left Grinding Gear Games in 2023, released a video over the weekend where he broke down everything Blizzard has announced about the upcoming Diablo game, from its story to itemization and monster levels. And while he did have some nitpicks, it seems like he's cautiously optimistic that the Diablo series is headed in the right direction, because of the influence the seminal Diablo 2 seems to have on it so far.

Wilson is particularly fond of the new character and inventory screen, where items once again boast different sizes, along with stats that are more in line with Diablo 2. However, there are some modern choices, such as a flat DPS number on weapons, that rub him the wrong way. Still, he recognizes that Diablo 5 can't fully embrace Diablo 2's at-times clunky design.

"There's a bigger question if they're going to go all the way and risk alienating the modern audience that they've cultivated over the last couple of decades," he said. "I don't think they necessarily should. While selfishly it'd be amazing for them to make a new version of Diablo 2 just for me, I don't think they could justify an investment of that size for a game with a niche audience."

Instead, Wilson expects that Diablo V will try to adopt the best of both worlds, with a "modern ARPG that borrows heavily from Diablo 2, rather than a true return to the design philosophy of Diablo 2."

But even though the game is still a couple years away, according to Blizzard, Wilson thinks Diablo 5 is going to end up delayed. He says, "my best guess is the game won't be ready for spring 2029, but that's ok, delays happen and are normal in this industry. I can't count the amount of times I had to delay a Path of Exile League release and players were okay with it."

Diablo 4 Lord of Hatred and Paladin Class Screenshots

If anything, delaying Diablo 5 would give Diablo 4 more room to breathe. Just like a lot of players, Wilson feels like the early announcement of D5 is a sign that Blizzard is abandoing Diablo 4 – even if Blizzard itself has denied that in an interview with PC Gamer . Instead, Blizzard is going to keep developing the story with new seasons, the latest of which is a 30-year celebration of the franchise.

I've already spent almost 50 hours in Season 15 alone, and have been having a blast with all the nostalgic content Blizzard added this time around. Chris Wilson is less amused by it, saying, "to be honest, this event feels pretty distasteful to me," because "Diablo 4 was slowly building up to you being able to fight all the prime evils, then they introduce them all at once in a special event that isn't really tied to the games story."

Regardless, new seasons will continue to filter out to Diablo 4 over the next year and a half. Blizzard will also be adding Diablo 2's Amazon class to the game in a DLC pack early next year. Speaking of classes, the company has also revealed a handful of the classes coming to Diablo 5 , and that at launch the new game will apparently have more classes available than in any previous Diablo game. I'm just hoping they bring back the Demon Hunter from Diablo 3 .
